title: Units comparison to the reduction is locally surjective
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme and $i:X_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ its reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Write $\mathbf G_{m,X}$ for the sheaf of units [def-sc-gm-torsor] on the small etale site, as an abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. The canonical comparison $\varphi:i^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,X}\to\mathbf G_{m,X_{\mathrm{red}}}$, the transpose of restriction of units under the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], is an epimorphism of abelian sheaves (every section locally lifts).

source.place: Proof, Step 1 and the following Claim; proof text retained in the parent DAG node

proof.text: For an affine etale V over X, the base change of the reduction is the quotient by the extended nilradical ideal. Its generators are nilpotent; every finite sum of their multiples is nilpotent. The quotient is etale over the reduced scheme X_red, hence reduced. Thus that extended ideal is exactly the nilradical of V.

A unit modulo a nil ideal lifts to a unit: lift the unit and its inverse to a and b. Then ab=1+t for a nilpotent t, and a finite geometric series in -t inverts 1+t. Multiplying b by this inverse gives an inverse for a. Apply this to each affine etale object to see that G_m,X -> i_*G_m,X_red is locally surjective.

Reduction is a universal homeomorphism, so inverse and direct image give an exact equivalence of abelian sheaf categories. Its counit is an isomorphism; applying inverse image to the preceding epi and composing with the counit gives its adjoint varphi, still epi.
